tasks.title: Exact-layer builder discussion
tasks.body:
One thing I learned while building an accessibility checker for Framer: a score is not very useful if it leaves you hunting for the problem.

The useful loop is much smaller:

find one issue -> open it -> land on the exact layer -> fix it -> scan again.

I am still deciding what information should come first on each finding:

1. why it matters
2. the exact layer
3. a suggested fix

For me, the exact layer wins. This is the interaction I am testing in Ally Auditor.

What would help you most during a client handoff?

tasks.title: What five small Framer plugins taught me about useful product proof
tasks.body:
Building five small Framer plugins taught me that a feature list is weak proof. A useful demo has to show one uncomfortable moment, one product action, and one visible result.

For Loka that is reviewed copy returning to the right layer. For Ally Auditor it is a finding opening the exact layer. For Gaode Maps it is a store-locator workflow replacing repeated Code Component setup. For Site Pet it is a cited answer with a safe next action. For Polyglot AEO it is unfinished multilingual handoff work becoming visible.

The next step is measuring which proof creates real product use, not just likes.
